body.title: Chhipa Artisans and the River Dyes: The Sanganer Block-Printing Lineage
body.orientation: How skilled hand-carved teak blocks and mineral dyes turned a village outside Jaipur into a global textile heritage center.

hero.alt: Artisan carving intricate wooden printing blocks in Jaipur

paragraphs.text: Sanganer, located south of Jaipur, has been home to the Chhipa community of textile printers since royal patronage flourished in the 17th century under the Kachwaha rulers.
The craft relies on hand-carved sheesham and teak blocks dipped in vegetable and mineral mordants to print precise floral and paisley motifs on natural cotton cloth.
The mineral-rich waters of the local Sanjaria River and the arid Rajasthani sun were essential in giving Sanganer prints their characteristic crisp white backgrounds and fast natural colors.
Recognized with a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, Sanganer block printing preserves an unbroken guild knowledge system resistant to mechanized mass production.

claims.text: The Chhipa community in Sanganer received royal patronage under the Kachwaha dynasty.

evidence.excerpt: Sanganer printing gained prominence in the 17th century when the rulers of Jaipur encouraged craft communities to settle in the region.

claims.text: Artisans use multiple carved wooden blocks to layer intricate floral patterns on cotton.

evidence.excerpt: Hand-carved wooden blocks made of teak or sheesham are used to apply patterns in successive color layers.

claims.text: Local water chemistry and sunlight were vital factors in developing the print's color fastness.

evidence.excerpt: The water of the local river was credited with imparting brightness and luster to the dyed cloth during washing and drying.

claims.text: Sanganer hand block printing holds statutory Geographical Indication protection.

evidence.excerpt: Sanganeri hand block printing has received Geographical Indication (GI) status under Indian intellectual property law.
